title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 vs Claude Fable 5 on DeepSWE: Cost, Coding, and Routing
gist: On DeepSWE, Claude Fable 5 wins single-shot accuracy (69.7% pass@1) but is the most expensive rollout on the board at $21.63, 90x more than DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813's $0.24, and Pro overtakes at pass@4 (88.5% vs 84.1%). With the lowest per-task correlation of any pairing (0.39), Together AI argues for a Pro-first cascade escalating to Fable only on test failure, reaching 82.7% at $8.28 per task, thirteen points better than Fable alone for 62% less.

insights.claim: Running DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 first and escalating to Claude Fable 5 only when it fails solves 82.7% of DeepSWE tasks at $8.28 each, thirteen points above Fable alone (69.7%) and 62% cheaper than Fable's $21.63.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: The cascade dominates Fable alone on both accuracy and cost, the headline actionable result.
insights.quote: Run DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 first, escalate to Claude Fable 5 only when it fails. That cascade solves 82.7% of DeepSWE tasks at $8.28 each.

insights.claim: The cascade beats a perfect one-shot oracle router (78.8%), and order is not optional: Pro-first costs $8.28 while Fable-first costs $21.71 for the same accuracy.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Leading with the cheap model is a large free cost saving with identical accuracy.
insights.quote: The order is not optional: Pro-first costs $8.28, Fable-first costs $21.71, for the same accuracy.

insights.claim: The best use of Fable is not as a default but as a selective escalation behind a low-cost Pro first stage, paid only on the handful of tasks that actually need a Rust or serialization specialist.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Reframes an expensive flagship as a targeted escalation tier rather than a default engine.

insights.claim: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 costs $0.24 per rollout versus Claude Fable 5's $21.63, a 90x gap that is the widest of any pairing measured, yielding 260 solves per $100 against Fable's 3.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Fable is the single most expensive config on the board, forcing a hard justification for its use.
insights.quote: Per $100 spent, Pro solves 260 tasks and Fable solves 3.

insights.claim: Unusually, Fable's 90x price does not come with a speed penalty for Pro: Fable's median rollout is 31 minutes to Pro's 35, roughly even, because Fable is the most verbose model on the board (115k output tokens) despite fewer steps (79 vs 146).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Fable cannot even claim a latency edge, removing the usual excuse for a premium model.
insights.quote: Pro takes more steps; Fable writes more per step. Neither model is notably faster.

insights.claim: Claude Fable 5 leads single-shot at 69.7% pass@1 vs Pro's 62.8%, but Pro pulls level at pass@2 (78.5 vs 77.1) and clears Fable at pass@4 by more than four points (88.5% vs 84.1%).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Fable's first-shot lead evaporates under retries, so it neither owns the ceiling nor holds its edge.
insights.quote: For a model that costs ninety times as much, Fable neither owns the ceiling nor holds its first-shot edge under retries.

insights.claim: Both models regress the existing test suite in only 11% of failures, well below the GPT-family's 20%, but Fable carries the largest big-miss share at 18% versus Pro's 10%, meaning Fable's wrong answers are more often badly wrong.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Both are safe to accept without heavy gating, but Fable's misses are the more expensive kind to debug.
insights.quote: when Fable is wrong it is more often badly wrong, a solution far off the mark rather than one edge case short.

insights.claim: Fable wins 6 of 8 domains led by data modeling and serialization at 88% (24 points over Pro), but Pro takes stateful reactivity (66 vs 64) and concurrency and durability (58 vs 45), a 13-point edge in exactly Fable's weakest domain.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: On concurrency the cheaper model is the better engineer, not just cheaper, narrowing Fable's real advantage.
insights.quote: Fable's 45% on concurrency is its weakest cell and the one domain where the lower-cost model is simply the better engineer, not just the cheaper one.
insights.locator: Where each wins, by task type

insights.claim: The number that justifies Fable's price is Rust at 85% to Pro's 65, a 20-point margin and the widest single gap in the matchup, but elsewhere it is closer than the price implies and Pro even takes TypeScript (61 vs 57).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Outside Rust and serialization the case for paying 90x is hard to make.
insights.quote: Outside Rust and serialization, the case for paying 90x is hard to make.

insights.claim: Per-task correlation is just 0.39, the lowest of any DeepSeek-Pro pairing measured; both solve 88 tasks, Pro alone gets 12, Fable alone gets 7, only 6 defeat both, and their union covers 107 of 113 tasks (94.7%).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Maximum divergence plus near-total union coverage is precisely what makes routing between them pay off.
insights.quote: That disagreement is the whole reason routing works.
insights.locator: Key Takeaways / How different are they

insights.claim: The disagreements go both ways: Pro sweeps awilix-async-container-initialization four-for-four while Fable never lands it, and Fable four-for-fours four tasks Pro zeros, evidencing real complementarity not redundancy.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Genuine two-way complementarity confirms the pair is a portfolio, not two views of the same capability.
insights.quote: This is real complementarity, not redundancy.

insights.claim: Fable 5 is the hardest single model on the board to justify as a default given the most expensive rollout, a first-shot lead retries erase, and no four-shot ceiling advantage; buy it only for Rust (85%) and serialization-heavy work (88%).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Narrows Fable's defensible use to two specialties, otherwise steering buyers to Pro or the cascade.

insights.claim: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 offers near-Fable first-try accuracy, a higher ceiling, an equal or better failure profile, and 90x lower cost, though it cedes Rust and the exact-contract domains.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: For high-volume or retry-tolerant agent work Pro is the stronger value pick.
